templates.title: Character
templates.description: Person which the player can control using the analog stick

params.note: Correct the character's posture while resting.
The character's legs should only animate when the character is walking, so it adds its walk speed to a number to track how far it's moved, and changes its art frame by that number.
This character is controlled by the player, and can be used as a template for your own character designs.

templates.title: Tracking Camera
templates.description: Makes the card’s viewport follow the character

params.note: This camera blueprint is a way of moving around the card's viewport to follow the player character, so that the character never leaves the edge of the screen. Just drop it into the card scene and it will follow the Character!

templates.title: Creature
templates.description: Walks in the opposite direction whenever it collides with something

params.note: Flip to face the direction that the actor is moving in
Make sure the actor is always moving

This mechanical mouse will pace back and forth, tapping any walls to its left and right. It will bounce off of the player, but you could change it to hurt the player instead with a little effort by changing its rules.

When the sparkle animation is over
Wave the actor up and down so that it looks like it's floating!
This floating gem is the player character's main objective. As the player collects it, it will increase the variable number named "$gems" of any #gemcounter actor by 1.

templates.title: Score Counter
templates.description: Text that counts up how many collectibles have been found

params.note: In Castle, when you write a variable's name preceded by a $ sign into a text actor, the text actor automagically knows to show that variable's number value at that spot in the text. This score actor uses this feature to display the amount of $gems that the player has collected!
